page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-standard-2 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the n2d family. It features 2 vCPUs mapped to a single physical core with 2 threads per core, utilizing dedicated CPU allocation. The underlying processor is an AMD EPYC 7B13 based on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include any local storage or bundled GPUs, and it comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data reveals a significant divergence between single-core and multi-core performance. The AMD EPYC 7B13 processor demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests, placing in the top 25%. However, multi-core CPU performance falls into the bottom 25% due to the limited physical core count. Memory performance is a notable bottleneck; the passmark memory score and cached small-block read bandwidth both rank in the bottom 10%, with uncached large-block read and write bandwidths registering in the bottom 25%. Consequently, workloads requiring high memory throughput or parallel processing will experience performance constraints.

Given its hardware profile and benchmark results, the n2d-standard-2 is suited for lightweight, single-threaded tasks such as basic text processing and single-threaded compression, where it achieves average performance. Conversely, it is poorly suited for database operations, static web serving, software compilation, and multi-threaded applications, all of which scored in the bottom 10% of benchmarks. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this instance offers a low-cost entry point to dedicated AMD EPYC resources, but it presents a high performance-per-resource tradeoff for any parallelized or memory-intensive workloads.
